purpose: Machine-readable non-regression baseline for coordination hot paths.

items.title: Claim before deep context
items.observed_failure: Fresh workers spent minutes listing pins, G1/G2, heartbeats, returns and protocols before attempting authority.
items.invariant: Before first PIN/claim, a fresh /wc performs only bootstrap, beacon, one allocator read and bounded atomic claim attempts.

items.title: Surplus workers close cleanly
items.observed_failure: Workers with no assignment remained visible for minutes and could be mistaken for recoverable work.
items.invariant: No-PIN workers create no recovery debt and age out of Live's active list quickly.

items.title: Live publication cannot starve under commit bursts
items.observed_failure: cancel-in-progress caused repeated worker commits to cancel the feed publisher before it could publish.
items.invariant: The running Live publisher is never cancelled merely because a newer commit arrived; bursts coalesce through the pending run.

items.title: Only current authority appears active
items.observed_failure: Historical/superseded PIN generations inflated active/replacement counts.
items.invariant: Only the newest authoritative generation for a job is projected as its current owner; older generations remain history only.

items.title: Public /wc pointer cannot expand preclaim work
items.observed_failure: The public /wc pointer instructed workers to load Guide, Metabolism and page protocols before allocation, contradicting claim-first.
items.invariant: The public /wc pointer may route to canonical bootstrap and allocator but must not require unrelated deep protocols before ownership.

items.title: Prefer clean ready work over recovery archaeology
items.observed_failure: Workers entered expensive recovery validation while clean ready work was available.
items.invariant: Allocator and /wc rank ready work before recovery; stale recovery snapshots are never manually reconstructed preclaim.

items.title: Guide hydrates by relevance, not full-state ritual
items.observed_failure: Fresh /g required exhaustive queues/claims/runs/returns/heartbeats even when the request referenced one page, inbox item or bounded decision.
items.invariant: Guide loads identity + epoch + focus, resolves exact user referents, then expands only the relevant durable slice; raw global archaeology is fallback, not default.

items.title: Telemetry epoch cannot reset when ledger text changes
items.observed_failure: Using baseline file updated_at as telemetry activation would erase accumulated runtime samples whenever the ledger gained a new ratchet item.
items.invariant: Runtime measurement uses an explicit stable activation timestamp, independent from ordinary baseline edits.

items.title: Claim transport authorization must be explicit and fail fast
items.observed_failure: A fresh worker read one allocator but two claim CREATEs were blocked by tool authorization/safety controls, wasting most of a launch despite no job-level collision.
items.invariant: The canonical human invocation explicitly authorizes bounded reversible Prometeo writes; a transport-level claim block stops immediately and is never retried across multiple candidates.

items.title: Efficiency timing comes from durable repository events
items.observed_failure: A no-allocation receipt reused the launch timestamp even though the beacon and close commits were roughly 39 seconds apart, understating wasted time.
items.invariant: Runtime timing prefers Git commit time for beacon/claim/no-allocation persistence and treats model-authored timestamps as descriptive metadata, not the measurement clock.

items.title: Fast claim pins are complete before immutable create
items.observed_failure: A fresh /wc won an atomic G000001 with a minimal payload, then post-claim protocol loading revealed required immutable pin metadata was missing. Append-only pin semantics correctly forbade repairing that generation in place.
items.invariant: The compiled allocator supplies every mandatory portfolio pin field before CREATE; a fresh worker fills only bounded placeholders and never needs deep preclaim archaeology or post-create metadata repair.

items.title: Generation-fixed fixtures never enter ordinary next-generation recovery
items.observed_failure: A G000001-only contention fixture aged into replaceable state and the allocator offered G000002, producing ownership that could not satisfy the fixture contract.
items.invariant: Recovery generation semantics are machine-readable data. Fixed-generation work is excluded from ordinary G+1 recovery after its fixed generation exists, remains visible through a bounded attention route, and normal retry-safe work keeps G+1 recovery.

status_legend.RATCHETED: static guard and runtime evidence both exist
